candidates.label: Dawn-night oaths sufficient for perception followed by destroyed civilisations
candidates.definition: In 89:1-14: By the dawn and by ten nights and by the even number and the odd and by the night when it passes; is there not in all that an oath sufficient for one of perception; have you not considered how your Lord dealt with Aad, Iram who had lofty pillars the likes of whom had never been created in the land, and Thamud who carved out the rocks in the valley, and Pharaoh owner of the stakes; all of whom oppressed within the lands and increased therein the corruption; so your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment; indeed your Lord is in observation.

candidates.label: Human misreading of trial: generosity as honour, restriction as humiliation
